title: Order No. U-37584 — Order Order for Magnolia Water Utility Operating Company, LLC, ex parte.
text:
Order No. U-37584 
Page 1 
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

ORDER NUMBER U-37584 

MAGNOLIA WATER UTILITY 
OPERATING COMPANY, LLC, EX PARTE 

Docket No. U-37584, In re: Request for extension of Formula Rate Plan. 
(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session.) 

ORDER 
Background and Overview 
In this proceeding, Magnolia Water Utility Operating Company, LLC (“Magnolia” or the 
“Applicant”) is seeking a renewal and extension of its Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”). Magnolia’s 
initial FRP, approved by the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission” or “LPSC”) in 
Order No. U-35822,1 began with test year 2022 and expired with test year 2024, having a Return 
on Equity (“ROE”) bandwidth of 9.00% to 10.00% and a 9.50% ROE midpoint.2 Magnolia seeks 
an extension of its FRP in its entirety. 
Commission Staff recommends that Magnolia be authorized to renew its FRP for an 
additional three-year term under the same terms and conditions as in its previously approved FRP, 
with certain language modifications and changes to its capital structure requirements. Intervenors 
in the docket, who are Magnolia customers, oppose Magnolia’s request. Generally, the Intervenors 
contend that Magnolia’s annual FRP filings, and Commission Staff’s analysis thereof, were 
incomplete and based on unsubstantiated financial reports of expenses and repairs. 

Pertinent Procedural History 
On May 16, 2025, Magnolia filed with the Commission a Request for Extension of Formula 
Rate Plan, with attached testimony in support (the “Request”). The Request was published in the 
Commission’s Official Bulletin on May 23, 2025, with a 15-day intervention period. There were 
twenty-five timely interventions.3 A status conference on the matter was held on July 8, 2025, at 
which a procedural schedule was established.

On October 27, 2025, Intervenors Connie Norris and Anne Pautler each filed their direct 
testimony/comments.

On January 27, 2026, individual pre-hearing statements were filed by Commission Staff, 
Magnolia, Ms. Case-Brown, and Ms. Pautler. On January 28, 2026, a Notice of Required Filing

Order No. U-37584 
Page 4 
The Administrative Law Judge issued a Proposed Recommendation on May 6, 2026. On 
May 14, 2026, Ms. Case-Brown filed her Exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation. On May 
20, 2026, Ms. Norris filed her Exceptions and Opposition to the Proposed Recommendation. On 
May 21, 2026, Magnolia filed its Oppositions to the Exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation. 
The Final Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge was issued on June 10, 2026. The 
Commission considered the Final Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge at its June 
17, 2026 Business and Executive Session. After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, 
seconded by Commissioner Francis, with Vice Chairman Coussan and Commissioner Lewis 
concurring, and Commissioner Campbell absent, the Commission voted to approve the Final 
Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge filed into the record on June 10, 2026. 

Jurisdiction and Applicable Law 
Pursuant to the Louisiana Constitution, Article 4, Section 21, the Commission shall 
regulate all common carriers and public utilities, and adopt and enforce reasonable rules, 
regulations, and procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties. La. R.S. 45:1163(A)(1) 
provides that the Commission shall exercise all necessary power and authority over any electric 
light, heat, power, or other local public utility “for the purpose of fixing and regulating the rates 
charged or to be charged by and service furnished by such public utilities.” La. R.S. 45:1164(A) 
states that the Commission’s power, authority, and duties “shall affect and include all matters and 
things connected with, concerning, and growing out of the service to be given or rendered by such 
public utility.” 

Summary of Parties' Positions 
Magnolia 

Magnolia argues that all credible evidence and testimony submitted in this proceeding 
supports the adoption of the Commission Staff’s Report and Recommendation that Magnolia’s 
FRP should be renewed with certain modifications. Magnolia opines that arguments presented by 
the Intervenors are frivolous and unsupported. Magnolia maintains that the allegations of 
substandard water service are completely unsupported, and in fact, the Louisiana Department of 
Health (“LDH”) has given Magnolia’s systems a community water system grade of “A” or “B”. 
Magnolia points out that the LDH letter grades are based on seven standards which evaluate 
infrastructure, accountability, and overall health risk of drinking water to consumers. Magnolia 
also maintains that the allegations of excessive rates disregard the significant capital investments 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 5 
that Magnolia has made in failing water and wastewater systems. Further, Magnolia points out that 
the capital investments were all reviewed and approved by the Commission prior to being included 
as a recoverable expense in Magnolia’s rates. Finally, Magnolia argues that the allegation of 
Magnolia not being transparent with regard to its finances is unsupported as Magnolia has 
willingly provided its full financial records, including audited financial statements, to Commission 
Staff each time it requested authorization to acquire a water and/or wastewater system, filed its 
annual FRP reports, or otherwise sought a rate adjustment. 

In its Opposition to the Exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation, Magnolia argues 
that Ms. Case-Brown made no new arguments and presented no new evidence in the Exceptions. 
Magnolia contends that Ms. Case-Brown’s arguments that Magnolia’s Request is procedurally 
defective is specious and is a logical fallacy because it presupposes some Commission rule that 
bars “late-filed” requests. Magnolia further counters that Ms. Case-Brown’s argument that 
Magnolia failed to produce audited financial statements is false, as those documents were produced 
for viewing to her. Magnolia also contends that Ms. Case-Brown argues that she was denied due 
process without articulating how she was denied such due process. Additionally, Magnolia asserts 
that the Tribunal’s determination on the scope of the proceeding is correct, as any expansion of 
the docket would have been improper. Finally, Magnolia points out that any water quality concerns 
were properly directed to the Louisiana Department of Health. 

Commission Staff 

Commission Staff believes that Magnolia’s Request is in the public interest and 
recommends that Magnolia’s Request be adopted, subject to certain conditions. Commission 
Staff’s conditions are that: 1) Magnolia be authorized to renew its FRP for an additional three 
years, subject to language modifications and a change to Magnolia’s imputed capital structure to 
52% equity and 48% debt; 2) Magnolia file into the record a revised tariff after an issuance of an 
Order in this docket; 3) Magnolia include a status update of all completed and pending capital 
improvement projects; 4) Magnolia include Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality 
(“LDEQ”) and LDH compliance documents with their annual filing; 5) Magnolia include a status 
update of all line-item surcharges approved by the Commission in each annual filing; and 6) upon 
the expiration of this FRP, Magnolia shall file for a full rate review with the Commission. 
Commission Staff asserts that Magnolia’s Request, subject to the changes recommended, provides 
for regular review of Magnolia’s situation, provides Commission Staff the ability to find errors 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 6 
and adjust/remove them from rate base, provides the ability to question and demand explanations 
for various projects, provides the ability to ascertain whether Magnolia is in compliance with 
LDEQ and LDH, and provides Commission Staff the ability to reduce rate shock due to large rate 
increases. Commission Staff points out that it has used the FRP mechanism for multiple companies 
to ensure that the companies have enough capital to provide service to meet all regulatory 
requirements. 

Commission Staff argues that the issues presented as contested by the Intervenors are either 
unrelated to this proceeding, or have already been decided by the Commission. Specifically, 
Commission Staff points out issues related to Commission Docket Nos. U-35822 and U-37570 
that have already been addressed, as those dockets have been voted upon by the Commission and 
orders have been issued. Additionally, Commission Staff maintains that certain discovery matters 
presented as contested issues by the Intervenors are evidentiary issues which have already been 
addressed in this proceeding. While Commission Staff acknowledges that water quality issues are 
valid concerns, Commission Staff maintains that LDH and LDEQ are the correct agencies to 
address these concerns. According to Commission Staff, it has no reason to believe, based upon 
the 242 systems removed from the LDEQ Administrative Order on Consents (“AOC”) and the 
positive grades from LDH, that Magnolia is providing substandard water quality. 

In response to other issues presented by the Intervenors, Commission Staff opines that it 
already recommended that Magnolia look into alternative or tiered billing to lessen the impact on 
lower usage customers, and that Magnolia personnel could be more proactive in providing updates 
to customers, including reviewing its notification system. Commission Staff points out that 
Magnolia is required to annually report to the Commission its current condition, both financial and 
actual, including the financial books, ratemaking adjustments, bank statements, ledgers, invoices, 
receipts, contracts, etc. Commission Staff maintains that these annual reviews allow the 
Commission Staff to review their accuracy and adjust them in line with Commission and industry 
standards. 

Intervenors 
Included are summaries of positions of Intervenors who filed briefs or testified at the hearing. 

Cindy Case-Brown 

Ms. Case-Brown informs that she is a resident of Greenleaves subdivision, whose water 
and sewer services have been provided by Magnolia since 2019. Ms. Case-Brown opposes 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 7 
Magnolia’s request for a three-year extension of its FRP. Ms. Case-Brown contends that the rates 
paid by Greenleaves residents for water and sewer services have dramatically increased since 
Magnolia acquired the Greenleaves system, without any substantial improvement in the quality or 
reliability of services. Ms. Case-Brown asserts that Magnolia has failed to meet its burden of proof 
in this matter. Ms. Case-Brown contends that: Magnolia has failed to comply with an order to 
produce documents relevant to its Request; Magnolia’s Request was untimely and without the 
required documentation; and the Commission Staff’s testimony demonstrated a lack of proper 
regulatory scrutiny. 
Ms. Case-Brown alleges that the FRP prioritized the growth of Magnolia over ratepayer 
protection, and that the rate increases are not sustainable. Ms. Case-Brown argues that Magnolia’s 
request should be denied because of willful misconduct, pervasive accounting errors, lack of fiscal 
responsibility, disregard of whether costs were prudently incurred, and disregard for public 
interest. Further, according to Ms. Case-Brown, Magnolia failed to meet its burden due to missing, 
inaccurate, and inconsistent documentation, as well as deficiencies in its books and recordkeeping. 
Ms. Case-Brown argues that excessive investment, significant capital spending, and wasteful 
duplication, all without meaningful regulatory scrutiny, is not in the interest of the public. Ms. 
Case-Brown asserts that the Commission should deny Magnolia’s request for an extension of its 
FRP, order Magnolia to undergo a full rate case, and order a full review of Magnolia’s previous 
applications and requests. 

In her exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation, Ms. Case-Brown alleges that the 
Proposed Recommendation contains multiple legal errors, unsupported conclusions, and internal 
inconsistencies that materially affect the outcome of this proceeding. Ms. Case-Brown contends 
that those deficiencies include: failure to enforce mandatory filing deadlines, failure to resolve 
material evidentiary issues, inadequate treatment of due process violations, improper narrowing of 
the scope of review, improper deferral of service quality issues, failure to properly apply the burden 
of proof, and reliance on incomplete or unverified data. Ms. Case-Brown argues that the Proposed 
Recommendation is not supported by substantial evidence, contains legal and procedural errors, 
and fails to adequately address critical issues raised by the Intervenors. 

Cindy Norris 

Ms. Norris contends that Magnolia’s Request is unsupported, unlawful, and contrary to the 
public interest. Ms. Norris argues that Magnolia’s Request suffers from multiple fatal defects that 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 8 
render it incomplete and legally insufficient for Commission review. Ms. Norris maintains that the 
Commission cannot evaluate, extend, or approve an FRP based on a filing that fails to meet the 
minimum evidentiary and procedural requirements. Ms. Norris argues that Magnolia has not 
produced the audited financial statements necessary for evaluating revenue requirements, capital 
expenditures, and affiliate transactions, and it has not demonstrated that its costs were prudently 
incurred or that its operational practices meet Commission standards. 
Ms. Norris argues that the record demonstrates that Magnolia has failed to provide safe, 
adequate, and reliable water service as required by Louisiana law and Commission regulations. 
Ms. Norris maintains that the unsafe service conditions documented in this docket demonstrate a 
pattern of neglect, mismanagement, and failure to comply with State and Commission 
requirements. 

Ms. Norris also argues that Magnolia failed to produce audited financial statements 
necessary for a prudence review, and failed to produce chain-of-custody documentation and 
operational-authority records. Ms. Norris contends that the absence of audited financials raises 
concerns regarding transparency, accuracy, and the potential for improper cost allocations among 
affiliates. Ms. Norris opines that the Commission cannot approve a renewal of the FRP without 
verified financial data demonstrating that Magnolia’s costs are reasonable, necessary, and 
prudently incurred. 

Ms. Norris also contends that the procedural posture of this docket has been marked by 
irregularities, refusals of evidence, missing filings, and Commission Staff inaction which 
materially prejudiced intervenors and prevented the creation of a complete and accurate record. 
Ms. Norris points out that Commission Staff failed to compel the production of audited financial 
statements, chain-of-custody documentation, and operational-authority records, despite their 
necessity for a prudence review and for evaluating Magnolia’s Request. Ms. Norris contends that 
due process requires transparency, access to evidence, and a fair opportunity for intervenors to 
participate meaningfully in the proceeding. According to Ms. Norris, the cumulative procedural 
defects in this docket constitute a denial of due process and independently justify denial of 
Magnolia’s request. 

Ms. Norris maintains that the Commission has both the authority and the obligation to 
ensure that regulated utilities operate transparently, comply with filing requirements, and provide 
the information necessary for Staff and intervenors to evaluate their requests. Accordingly, Ms. 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 9 
Norris opines that the Commission should deny Magnolia’s Request, declare Magnolia’s filing 
incomplete and non-compliant, and require submission of audited financial statements prior to any 
future FRP filings. Ms. Norris argues that approving Magnolia’s Request without audited 
financials would set a dangerous precedent, which would erode regulatory discipline and invite 
future noncompliance across the utility sector. 
In her exceptions to the Proposed Recommendation, Ms. Norris argues that the Proposed 
Recommendation contains significant procedural, evidentiary, and legal errors that prevent it form 
serving as a reliable basis for Commission action. According to Ms. Norris, those errors include: 
1) the omission of material evidence; 2) the misapplication of the burden of proof; 3) the 
acceptance of unsupported assertions; 4) the failure to address the contamination and service 
quality failures; 5) the exclusion of Central States Water Resources, Inc. (“CSWR”) and affiliate 
financials; 6) the failure to apply the Commission’s 1994 General Order; 7) the failure to apply the 
TESI stipulations and Order Nos. U-35822 and U-35322; and 8) the failure to enforce the 3 year 
FRP term and mandatory full rate case requirement. Ms. Norris seeks that the Proposed 
Recommendation be rejected or modified, that the Commission require a complete review of the 
financials of CSWR and its affiliates, that the 1994 General Order, the TESI stipulations and Order 
Nos. U-35822 and U-35322 be applied, that the FRP expiration date be enforced, that the 
Commission require a full rate case, and that the Commission consider issues relating to 
contamination, service quality and ratepayer impact. 

Anne Pautler 

Ms. Pautler claims that Magnolia has not provided sufficient quantifiable information to 
support their Request, and the narratives by Magnolia representatives are insufficient to support 
Magnolia’s Request. Ms. Pautler is concerned that the Commission will adopt recommendations 
based on unsubstantiated financial reports of expenses and repairs. Ms. Pautler argues that it is not 
possible to achieve fair and reasonable rates without accurate cost calculations and prudent 
spending. Ms. Pautler contends that Magnolia began operations in Louisiana with the intent of 
aggressive growth, but has demonstrated neglect by not fully meeting the needs of their customers. 
Ms. Pautler argues that clean, reliable, safe drinking water should come before any rate increases. 
Ms. Pautler asserts that Magnolia has not provided sufficient evidence to prove their claims of 
meeting public interest nor have they made a reasonable effort to solve customer grievances. 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 10 
Additionally, Ms. Pautler argues that she was denied participation in Docket No. U-37570 
due to issues with data requests in that proceeding. Ms. Pautler contends that the Commission Staff 
practiced a lack of due diligence in this matter and Docket No. U-37570, which resulted in the 
intervenors not receiving their due process. Ms. Pautler argues that Order No. U-37570 should be 
withdrawn, and the Commission should immediately halt all pending and future acquisitions by 
Magnolia. Ms. Pautler asserts that contrary to Magnolia’s contention that more connections result 
in lower and stable rates, Magnolia has the most connections of all private equity water utilities 
yet has the highest residential rate. 

Findings of Fact 
Magnolia, a Louisiana limited liability company, is a Commission regulated, for-profit utility 
providing water and wastewater service to approximately 55,552 wastewater connections and 
approximately 21,873 water connections in 33 parishes throughout Louisiana. Magnolia Request 
at 1 (Magnolia Hr’g Ex. 1); Pendergrass Direct at 3 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia is part of an affiliate group that includes its parent company, Central States Water 
Resources, Inc., a Missouri corporation, and several other operating companies, which operate 
small water and/or wastewater utilities in Missouri, Kentucky, Louisiana, Texas, Tennessee, 
Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Arizona, and Arkansas. Magnolia Request 
at 1 (Magnolia Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia’s current rates were set pursuant to its initial FRP, established through Commission 
Order No. U-35822. Magnolia Request at 2 (Magnolia Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia’s initial FRP began with test year 2022 and expired with test year 2024, utilizing an 
earnings bandwidth based on a calculated Return on Equity (“ROE”) lower limit of 9.00%, an 
upper limit of 10.00%, and a midpoint of 9.50%. Magnolia Request at 2 (Magnolia Hr’g Ex. 1); 
Pendergrass Direct at 3 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

If Magnolia earnings were to fall above the upper limit of the bandwidth, then a rate change would 
occur to bring Magnolia down to the upper limit of 10.00%. If Magnolia earnings were to fall 
below the lower limit of the bandwidth, then a rate change would occur to bring Magnolia up to 
the lower limit of 9.00%. Pendergrass Direct at 3 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia was required to file its FRP Annual Report on or before May 1 of each of the years 2023, 
2024, and 2025, containing a calculation of Magnolia’s revenue requirement based on the twelve 
months ending December 31 of the previous year. Staff Report and Recommendation at 3 
(Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia was required to use an imputed capital structure for its ROE calculations for the 2022 
and 2023 Test Years of 40% debt and 60% equity, or higher amount if the actual debt level was 
higher than 40% at the end of the Test Year. For the 2025 Test Year, Magnolia was required to 
use an imputed capital structure of 50% debt and 50% equity for ROE calculations. Staff Report 
and Recommendation at 4 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia was required to create a System Acquisition Regulatory Asset (“SARA”) on its balance 
sheet whereby it would accrue any operating losses during the test year. Staff Report and 
Recommendation at 4 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 11 
A review of Magnolia’s annual FRP filing for the 2022 Test Year was conducted in Docket No. 
U-36790. Staff Report and Recommendation at 6 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Docket No. U-36790 was considered and decided at the Commission’s October 18, 2023 Business 
and Executive Session, with Order No. U-36790 being issued on November 16, 2023. Order No. 
U-36790. 

A review of Magnolia’s annual FRP filing for the 2023 Test Year was conducted in Docket No. 
U-37191. Staff Report and Recommendation at 7 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Docket No. U-37191 was considered and decided at the Commission’s August 14, 2024 Business 
and Executive Session, with Order No. U-37191 being issued on August 29, 2024. Order No. U-
37191. 

A review of Magnolia’s annual FRP filing for the 2024 Test Year was conducted in Docket No. 
U-37570. Staff Report and Recommendation at 8 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Docket No. U-37570 was considered and decided at the Commission’s August 20, 2025 Business 
and Executive Session, with Order No. U-37570 being issued on September 19, 2025. Order No. 
U-37570. 

During the three-year span from 2022 to 2024, Magnolia's earnings fell outside of the bandwidth 
resulting in a decrease in water rates once and an increase two times, and an increase in sewer rates 
all three years. Staff Report and Recommendation at 9 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Magnolia’s base water rates increased by 38% and sewer rates increased by 30% from the initial 
rate case in 2020. Staff Report and Recommendation at 9 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Total water customers increased by 86% and sewer customers, increased by 144% from the initial 
rate case in 2020. Staff Report and Recommendation at 9 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Commission Staff prepared a Capital Asset Pricing Model (“CAPM”) to determine whether 
Magnolia’s current authorized ROE is still within a reasonable range. Staff Report and 
Recommendation at 9 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

After analyzing the CAPM, Commission Staff determined that the current authorized ROE is 
justified and will allow Magnolia the opportunity to earn a fair return on its investments. Staff 
Report and Recommendation at 11 (Commission Staff Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Commission Staff recommends that Magnolia be required to use an imputed capital structure for 
the term of its FRP of 52% equity and 48% debt, based on the average capital structure of the 
proxy companies in the CAPM. Staff Report and Recommendation at 11 (Commission Staff Hr’g 
Ex. 1). 

Analysis 
In the instant matter, Magnolia seeks an extension of the initial FRP for an additional three-
year term, effective with Magnolia’s December 31, 2025 test year and extending through the 
December 31, 2027 test year, with all material provisions left unchanged.6 Magnolia’s initial FRP 

6 Magnolia Request at 2 (Magnolia Hr’g Ex. 1). 

Order No. U-37584 
Page 12 
was established through Commission Order No. U-35822.7 While the parties have presented many 
issues as contested, the inquiry in the proceeding is limited to whether Magnolia should be granted 
an extension of its current FRP. 
Generally, an FRP is a ratemaking method that allows for annual rate adjustments outside 
of a general rate case.8 In ratemaking, the Commission seeks to establish just and reasonable rates 
to be charged by a public utility.9 The general rule is that the proponent of the agency action bears 
the burden of proof.10 Therefore, Magnolia has the burden of proof in this proceeding to show that 
the extension of its FRP would result in the setting of just and reasonable rates. If Magnolia 
establishes that, then the burden shifts to the opposing party to present sufficient evidence to 
overcome Magnolia’s case.11 

In support of its request, Magnolia presented into evidence its Application with the Pre-
Filed Direct Testimony of Josiah Cox, the Pre-Hearing Brief of Magnolia, and the live testimony 
of Josiah Cox at the hearing. Mr. Cox is the President of Magnolia, and also the President of 
Central States Water Resources, Inc. (“CSWR”).12 Magnolia and CSWR are part of an affiliated 
group of companies that provide water and/or wastewater utility services to customers in Missouri, 
Kentucky, Louisiana, Texas, Tennessee, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, 
Arizona, and Arkansas.13 Mr. Cox testified that Magnolia’s Louisiana business operations began 
in 2019, when Magnolia was qualified as a regulated water and wastewater utility.14 Magnolia 
started business operations with the acquisition of four systems in St. Tammany Parish, 
Louisiana.15 According to Mr. Cox, Magnolia has over 200 employees in Louisiana, and it also 
uses third-party contractors in its operations.16 

Mr. Cox testified that Magnolia is regulated by the Commission, LDH, LDEQ, and various 
local agencies.17 At the hearing Mr. Cox provided an overview of the various consent decrees

Intervenors have made several complaints regarding Magnolia’s water quality. LDEQ 
regulates various environmental matters, including air quality, water quality, solid and hazardous 
waste, transportation of sewage sludge, and public health and safety; however, LDEQ's water 
regulation relates to Louisiana's bodies of water, not drinking water.50 LDH, through the state 
health officer, prepares the rules and regulations necessary to ensure that water supplied to the 
public by public water supplies is obtained from safe and sanitary sources and that there are 
standards for drinking water quality, water works construction, and water works operations.51 
Additionally, LDH is responsible for monitoring water samples, inspecting sites, reviewing 
engineering plans prior to issuing permits, providing guidance and resources for water quality 
maintenance, and informing the public about health advisories.52 Therefore, whether a utility meets 
standards for drinking water quality is a determination to be made by LDH. Further, LDH has the 
Safe Drinking Water Program, which develops a grade for community water systems. LDH 
determines letter grades based on standards evaluating the infrastructure, accountability, and 
overall health risk of drinking water to consumer. Sixty-one of Magnolia’s systems have a grade 
of “A,” and four of its systems have a grade of “B.”53

Considering the totality of the evidence, Magnolia’s Request for an extension of its FRP, 
with the modifications recommended by Commission Staff, is appropriate. Commission Staff 
included in its recommendation that upon the expiration of the FRP Magnolia would file for a full 
rate review with the Commission in conjunction with its 2027 test year Annual Report filing. 
However, the redline proposed FRP attached to Ms. Pendergrass’ testimony states that “in the

Conclusion 
Based upon the analysis above, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED THAT: 
1) Magnolia be authorized to renew its FRP for an additional three-year term for the 2025, 
2026 and 2027 Test Years under the same terms and conditions as are in its previously 
approved FRP, with certain language modifications and changes to its capital structure 
requirements as outlined in the proposed FRP attached to Robin Pendergrass’ Direct 
Testimony filed on November 3, 2025, except as detailed below; 
2) The procedural deadlines for Magnolia’s 2025 Test Year FRP annual review shall be 
extended 30 days from the date of issuance of an Order in this proceeding; 
3) Magnolia shall file into the record of this proceedings, along with a copy to the 
Commission’s Utilities Division, a new or revised tariff reflecting the Commission’s 
action, within 30 days of issuance of an Order in this proceeding; 
4) Magnolia shall include with each annual review filing, a complete status update of all 
completed and pending capital improvement projects, along with all supporting 
documentation for Commission Staff review; 
5) Magnolia shall continue to maintain compliance with the LDH and LDEQ; 
6) Magnolia shall include with each annual FRP review filing, a complete status update of its 
open LDEQ Compliance Orders and LDH violations, along with all supporting 
documentation for Commission Staff review; 
7) Magnolia shall include with each annual FRP review filing, a complete status update of all 
line-itemed surcharges approved by this Commission, along with all supporting 
documentation for Commission Staff review; and 
8) Upon the expiration of this FRP, Magnolia shall file for a full rate review with the 
Commission in conjunction with its 2027 Test Year Annual Report filing.
